newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close little changed in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close little changed in light trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in very light trade on Tuesday, with the market focused largely on new supply and key Canadian and U.S. employment data due out on Friday, analysts said.

"It was just basically moving things back and forth between dealers as far as I could tell. I didn't see anything substantive," said one Toronto-based T-bill trader. "It was actually focused more on corporate new issues than anything."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.10 to C$115.80 to yield 6.715 percent against the U.S. 30-year bonds, which rose 2/32 to yield 6.36 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds was 36 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Monday.
The Canadian market was hit with a wave of new supply from corporations this morning, led by the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, which set a C$300 million, 4.5 percent bond due December 6, 1999.
Westcoast Energy Inc also entered the market, setting a C$125 million 6.45 percent bond due 2006 and a C$125 million 7.30 percent bond due 2026.
Dealers are anticipating the auction tomorrow of C$3.0 billion in two-year bonds by the Government of Canada.
The new bonds and expectations of new supply both weighed on the short end of the yield curve, analysts said.
Volume in the Canadian bond market is expected to remain light until the release on Friday of key U.S. and Canadian economic reports, dealers said.

"That's the kind of market you've got right now. Everybody is going to be pretty uncomfortable for a couple more days," said Tom Poff, vice-president of fixed-income investment with Mulvihill Capital Management Inc.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.03 to C$107.10 to yield 6.043 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.06 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was two basis points, unchanged from Monday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.77 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.02 percent.
